name: economy-director-getting-started
description: "Use on first run with a new owner: onboard them one question at a time, list what they provide, and run the first Game Economy Director grade with the lens engine."
---

> **Audit contract v1 (overrides everything below).** Created by @meta_alchemist (https://x.com/meta_alchemist).
> - Score only with the rubric embedded in `engine/lens.mjs` (`LENS.rubric`, gbf-06-game-economy-director v1.3.0). `node engine/lens.mjs <pack.json>` computes the grade; this skill only gathers evidence for it and never adds points of its own.
> - Missing evidence is UNMEASURED (0 points, not a defect). A test that did not run is NOT_RUN, never PASS. Never invent a measurement; label every worked example synthetic.
> - Game facts and budgets come from your game profile (`pack.profile`). Treat sample numbers as illustrative. Set the frame-time budget separately for each target device in your game profile.
> - An automated gate needs a negative fixture that fails. Receipts carry measured values, never an unconditional PASS.
> Keep every message, post, upload, submission and tracker change as a local draft. Only the human reviews and sends, publishes, uploads or files it. Work only on a working branch. Push only when the human asks and only to that branch. Never push to main. The human merges and deploys. Any feature switch you add is off by default.

# Game Economy Director: Getting Started

Model where your game's resources come from and where they go (sources and sinks), how long progression takes, and whether rewards are counted fairly. Combat timing and payment checks are optional modules for games that have them.

If `engine/lens.mjs`, `engine/lens-kit.mjs` or `fixtures/good-pack.json` are not on disk yet, write them byte for byte from the `economy-director-lens-engine` skill first (Node 18+, no dependencies).

## 1. Onboard one question at a time

Ask one question at a time, wait for the answer, then ask the next. Never stack questions in one message. Skip a question when an earlier answer already settled it.

1. Which game are we reviewing?
2. Which build should I grade?
3. Who or what produces the evidence pack for that build: a CI job or a manual playtest capture?
4. What do players earn and spend in your game? For example coins, wood, energy, lives, cards, crafting materials, keys or experience.
5. Where is progress saved: on the device, in the cloud, on a server, or more than one of these?
6. Does the game give random rewards, such as drops, card packs, chests or random harvests?
7. Does the game have combat? If not, we use the `no-combat` profile: I skip the combat timing module, its two lines read N/A, and their 20 points are shared over the other eight lines.
8. Does the game sell anything for real money (items, currency, a pass, an ad-free upgrade)? If not, we use the `no-store` profile: the paid-path and payment lines read N/A and their partner lines take each pillar's 20 points.
9. If it does sell something: do you have a store sandbox (a test mode with no real money) where you can try failed, duplicate and refunded purchases yourself? I only review your sandbox results; I never make a charge, refund or grant, real or sandbox.
10. How long should a typical player take to reach the next step of progression (a level, a farm upgrade, a city tier, a full card set)? This becomes `maxProgressStepDays`.
11. Then ask the remaining targets one per message, only for the systems the game has, starting from the synthetic values in `fixtures/good-pack.json`:
    - Random rewards: How wide may the 95 percent range around a reward rate be before you want more data? (`maxRewardIntervalWidth`)
    - Something for sale: Over the same period, what share of the paid path should a player who never pays still reach? (`minFreeShareOfPaid`)
    - Combat: What are the fastest and slowest acceptable median times to defeat a target? (`timeToDefeatBandS`)
    - Combat: How far may simulated fights differ from recorded ones? (`maxModelDeltaS`)
    - Combat: How large an error is acceptable when several attackers hit one target? (`maxMultiAttackerErrS`)
    - Combat: Do all attackers hit on the same beat, or will you export each hit's time and damage? (`combatModel`: `simultaneous` or `event-ledger`)
12. Who reviews the local finding drafts before anything is filed?

Read the profile picks back to the owner and, once they approve, set them before scoring, for example `"rubricProfile": ["no-combat", "no-store"]` in `pack.profile`.

Before grading a real pack, check that its build and profile match the owner's answers. Record a capture or run that could not happen as NOT_RUN. Use the sample sizes listed by `node engine/lens.mjs --meta`.

## 2. What you provide

- An evidence pack (JSON) with `status: "VALID"`, a `liveSha`, a `gitSha` and a `packId` (all three are required), and an `artifacts` list. Every metric group names the artifact id it came from.
- Metric groups this engine reads, by system:
  - Every game with resources: `progression` (static), `reachability` (trace), `rewards` (trace), `balance` (trace), `storage` (trace).
  - Random rewards: `randomRewards` (static).
  - Something for sale: `freeVsPaid` (static), `payments` (trace), and the growth checks `storePricing` (static) and `paidEdge` (static).
  - Combat: `timeToDefeat` (trace), `multiAttacker` (static).
- Profile thresholds in `pack.profile`. A missing threshold makes its line U, never a default.
- Anything you cannot capture yet stays out of the pack. It grades U (UNMEASURED), which is honest and costs no false defect. With `no-combat` or `no-store` approved, leave that system's groups out too; its lines read N/A.

## 3. Run the first grade

```
node engine/lens.mjs fixtures/good-pack.json   # worked example, synthetic, not a measurement
node engine/lens.mjs your-pack.json            # your build
node engine/lens.mjs --meta                    # rubric lines, weights and what each reads
node engine/lens.mjs --fixtures fixtures/good-pack.json  # negative and missing-input self-test
```

Read the record: `verdict` (PASS, CONDITIONAL, BLOCKED or INVALID), `grade` and `coverage`, then each line's `level` and `findings`, then `checks` (growth checks reported beside the grade) and `tickets` (deduplicated candidates).

## 4. Report in plain English

- Lead with the verdict, grade and coverage in one sentence. Say how much of the rubric was measured.
- List U lines as "not measured yet" with the capture that would measure them. Never call them defects. Name the rubric profiles used next to the grade. For a U line about a system the game does not have and no profile covers, write "does not apply: no random rewards" (or "one save path") instead.
- One local ticket draft per measured finding, with the pack id and artifact ids. Label any synthetic pack as synthetic.
- Rubric lines, grouped by what they need:
  - Every game with resources: progression:1, progression:2, reward-fairness:1, entitlement-consistency:2, loot-access:2 (it also reads the random reward group today).
  - Random rewards: loot-access:1.
  - Something for sale: reward-fairness:2, entitlement-consistency:1.
  - Combat: combat-balance:1, combat-balance:2.

## 5. Skills in this template

- `resource-sources-and-sinks-model`: start here. List every source and sink, model balances over time, and find stuck players, unreachable goals and double-counted rewards.
- `monte-carlo-meta-balancer`: run many seeded simulations of player choices to measure progression time, dominant choices and the effect of a proposed change.
- `combat-timing-auditor`: optional, only if the game has combat. Compare simulated and recorded time to defeat a target.
- `economy-director-lens-engine`: the engine source and how to run it.

## Lines that do not apply to your game

Two approved profiles live in `RUBRIC.json`. The owner approves them before scoring and you set them in `pack.profile.rubricProfile`:

- `no-combat` (no combat): `combat-balance:1` and `combat-balance:2` read N/A, and that pillar's 20 points are shared over the other eight lines (12.5 each). Leave `timeToDefeat`, `multiAttacker` and `receipts.modelInputs` out.
- `no-store` (sells nothing: no paid items, currency or access): `reward-fairness:2` and `entitlement-consistency:1` read N/A, and `reward-fairness:1` and `entitlement-consistency:2` take 20 each. Leave `freeVsPaid`, `payments`, `receipts.entitlementDrills`, `storePricing` and `paidEdge` out.

N/A is not U and not a defect, and with every other line at level 3 or more the verdict can be PASS. When both are selected the engine applies the same rule (see `docs/RUBRIC_GUIDE.md` in the kit, section Applicability). Never move weights during a run.

Random rewards (`loot-access:1`) and a second save path (`progression:2`) have no profile. A game without them leaves the line U, coverage drops below 100 percent and the verdict stays CONDITIONAL even when every measured line passes. Say in the report which U lines are "does not apply" so nobody reads them as missing work.

## Storage and payment drills (owner-run)

- Storage: the owner runs the same seeded actions on each supported save path in an isolated test copy and compares the saved state before and after (`receipts.storageReplay`, line `progression:2`).
- Payments, only for a game that sells something: the owner rehearses a declined, duplicate, interrupted and restored purchase with synthetic orders in the store sandbox and records expected versus actual grants and losses (`receipts.entitlementDrills`, line `entitlement-consistency:1`). Without these tests the line never passes.
- Production records are read-only. Only the human operates payments, grants or refunds.

## Blockers to tell the owner about

- For a game with purchases, payment failure evidence needs a sandbox account; the worked example is synthetic.

Before capture, agree on the case IDs and expected values in `profile.cases`. Run `node engine/lens.mjs --meta` for the required row fields and comparisons. Record one row per approved case under `receipts`, including its id, liveSha and artifact ID. A skipped or stale case leaves its line U. The bundled rows and budgets are synthetic.

# Combat timing (optional: only if your game has combat)

This is the one combat module in the economy template. Use it only when your game has fights where one side wears another down: a fighting game, a tower defence game, a turn-based RPG, a 3D arena game or a twin-stick shooter. It feeds two rubric lines: `combat-balance:1` (how long it takes to defeat a target) and `combat-balance:2` (what happens when several attackers hit one target).

If your game has no combat (a farming sim, a city builder, a card game scored by points, a puzzle game, a narrative adventure), stop here. Leave the `timeToDefeat` and `multiAttacker` groups out of the pack. With the owner's approval, set `"rubricProfile": ["no-combat"]` in the game profile before scoring: both lines read N/A, not U, and their 20 points are shared over the other eight lines. Never invent timing numbers to fill them.

## Words used here

- Time to kill (TTK): the time from the first hit until a target is defeated. In a turn-based game count turns instead of seconds and say so in `timeToDefeat.label`.
- Weapon: anything that deals damage, such as a sword, a spell, a tower type, a unit or a card. `timeToDefeat.perAttackP50S` holds one median (the middle value, P50) per weapon.
- Focus fire: several attackers hitting the same target.
- Combat model: the overlap rule your build really uses, set as `combatModel` in the game profile. `simultaneous` means every attacker hits on the same beat, with the first volley at time zero. `event-ledger` means you export each hit's time and the damage that actually applied.

## Method

1. Pick one fight with a clear start and end, for example one tower against one basic enemy, or one hero against one boss phase. Use the same units, start condition and rules as the game code.
2. Work out the expected time from the build's own numbers. For a repeated fixed hit, the number of hits is the target's health divided by damage per hit, rounded up. If the first hit lands at once, the elapsed time covers one fewer interval than the hit count. Add wind-up, recovery, reload or cooldown pauses only where the game's rules have them.
3. Simulate with the weapon definitions exported from the build (never hand-typed copies). Set `timeToDefeat.label` to say the numbers are simulated, and record the median time per weapon in `timeToDefeat.perAttackP50S`. Each median must sit inside the profile's `timeToDefeatBandS` range.
4. Compare the simulation with fights recorded in a playtest. Put the largest gap in `timeToDefeat.simVsRecordedMaxDeltaS`. Level 4 needs that gap within the profile's `maxModelDeltaS`.
5. Test the edges: a hit that lands exactly on zero health, a case that needs one extra hit, and misses if your game has a hit chance.
6. For focus fire, use only the rule the build has. Never add a damping factor or an attacker-count multiplier the game does not apply. Record examples in `multiAttacker.examples`. For each approved case in `profile.cases.modelInputs`, add one row to `receipts.modelInputs` that links the build config and an independently recorded timing trace. If damage is staggered, rounded or routed (for example through a shield first), use the `event-ledger` model and export each hit's time and applied damage in time order.

## Short examples (synthetic, for illustration only)

- Tower defence: a frost tower deals 20 per hit every 0.8 s to an enemy with 110 health. That is 6 hits; with the first hit at once, the enemy falls at 5 x 0.8 = 4.0 s.
- Turn-based RPG: a spell deals 30 to a foe with 100 health, so 4 turns. Set `timeToDefeat.label` to "simulated, turns".
- 3D arena game: two players each deal 20 every 0.5 s to a target with 100 health. With the `simultaneous` model that is 3 volleys, so 1.0 s, not a doubled or squared damage rate.
- Fighting game: a combo's simulated damage comes from the move data file, then gets checked against recorded rounds from a local playtest.

Thresholds (`timeToDefeatBandS`, `maxMultiAttackerErrS`, `maxModelDeltaS`, `combatModel`) come from the game profile. An unavailable config or trace leaves the line U.

Gather evidence for `node engine/lens.mjs <pack.json>`.

skills.name: resource-sources-and-sinks-model
skills.description: Start here for any game where players earn and spend something: list every source (where a resource comes from) and sink (where it goes), model balances over time, and find stuck players, unreachable goals and double-counted rewards.

description: "Start here for any game where players earn and spend something: list every source (where a resource comes from) and sink (where it goes), model balances over time, and find stuck players, unreachable goals and double-counted rewards."
---

> **Audit contract v1 (overrides everything below).** Created by @meta_alchemist (https://x.com/meta_alchemist).
> - Score only with the rubric embedded in `engine/lens.mjs` (`LENS.rubric`, gbf-06-game-economy-director v1.3.0). `node engine/lens.mjs <pack.json>` computes the grade; this skill only gathers evidence for it and never adds points of its own.

> Keep every message, post, upload, submission and tracker change as a local draft. Only the human reviews and sends, publishes, uploads or files it. Work only on a working branch. Push only when the human asks and only to that branch. Never push to main. The human merges and deploys. Any feature switch you add is off by default.

# Model resource sources and sinks

Start here for any game that has something players earn and spend: coins, wood, energy, lives, cards, crafting materials, keys or experience. A source adds a resource (a harvest, a quest reward, a level clear, a daily gift). A sink removes it (a purchase from a shop in the game, an upgrade, upkeep, repair, decay, a crafting cost). A transfer moves it between players or between resources without creating or destroying any.

## Method

1. Pick the unit (coins, wood, lives), the time step (a turn, a day in the game, a play session) and what carries over between sessions.
2. List every source and sink with its trigger, amount and who can use it. List transfers (trading, gifting, converting duplicates into crafting dust) separately.
3. For each step, closing balance = opening balance + inflows - outflows. Run low, typical and heavy play. Use measured activity from session logs where you have it, and label anything assumed.
4. Compare time to each goal, the share of players who get stuck and the balance at a few percentiles (for example the 10th, 50th and 90th) with the ranges the owner picked. Look at the low end, not only the average: a healthy total can hide players who cannot afford the next required step.
5. For each group of players and period, divide permanent outflow by generated inflow to see how much of the resource leaves the game. If nothing came in, the ratio is undefined: say so, do not report zero.
6. Change one assumption at a time and rerun.
7. Add two negative fixtures and confirm the output catches them: a zero-income player (an unreachable goal must show up) and a reward granted twice for one claim (a duplicate grant must show up).

## Short examples (synthetic, for illustration only)

- Farming or life sim: crop sales and foraging are sources; seeds, tool upgrades and house expansions are sinks; energy refills each morning up to a cap.
- City builder: taxes per citizen are a source; building upkeep is a sink; a bridge needed to unlock the next district is a required goal.
- Card game: packs earned from wins are a source; duplicates convert into crafting dust (a transfer); crafting a chosen card is a sink.
- Mobile puzzle game with boosters: coins per cleared level are a source; boosters and extra moves bought with coins are sinks; lives refill over time.
- Free game with no store: every resource is earned, and the model still finds stuck players and runaway hoards.
- Narrative adventure: keys and quest items are resources; spending the only key on the wrong door would make the story impossible to finish.

## What to put in the pack

- `progression`: `assumptionsStated` (at least two, for example minutes played per day and success rate) and `stepDaysEstimate` (days to reach the next step of progression: a level, a farm upgrade, a city tier, a full card set). It must stay within the profile's `maxProgressStepDays`. For each approved case in `profile.cases.simulationRun`, add a row to `receipts.simulationRun` with the player group, seed, horizon, repetitions, config and the low, estimate and high days. Feeds `progression:1`.
- `reachability`: `requiredPaths` (goals every player must be able to reach) and `unreachable` (how many cannot be reached). Feeds `loot-access:2`. That line also reads the `randomRewards` group today, so a game with no random rewards sees it as U; say so in the report.
- `randomRewards` (only if your game has random rewards such as drops, card packs, chests or random crop yields): `drops` (total rolls observed), `rare` (how many gave the outcome you track) and `intervalsReported` (true when the report shows a 95 percent range around the rate, not only the rate). The range must be no wider than the profile's `maxRewardIntervalWidth`. Feeds `loot-access:1`.
- `rewards`: `retriesSimulated` (at least 10 repeated claims of the same reward) and `duplicateGrantsA` and `duplicateGrantsB` (extra grants seen on each save path, for example local save and cloud save). Feeds `reward-fairness:1`.
- `balance`: `operations` (at least 20 earn or spend actions) and `mismatches` (times the number shown to the player differed from the saved or server value). Feeds `entitlement-consistency:2`.

Thresholds come from the game profile. A group you cannot measure stays out of the pack and its line grades U.

Gather evidence for `node engine/lens.mjs <pack.json>`.

# Simulate player choices and balance changes

Monte Carlo simulation means running the same scenario many times with different random seeds and looking at the spread of results, not one lucky or unlucky run. The "meta" is the set of choices players settle on as the strongest. This skill checks whether a balance change keeps several choices worth picking and how long progress really takes.

## Method

1. Define the choices, the outcome you measure and a realistic mix of player behaviour. Version the rules, seeds and behaviour weights with the experiment.
2. Run the current rules and the proposed rules on the same seeds, so each pair of runs differs only in the change. Use enough runs for the precision you need.
3. For each choice, report the number of runs, completions divided by attempts, the spread of completion times (percentiles) and a range (interval) around each estimate. A choice nobody tried has no success rate; say so.
4. For choice diversity, compute normalized entropy from the observed choice shares when at least two choices exist: 1 means players spread evenly, near 0 means one choice dominates.
5. Check strong combinations on their own. If a choice is only dominant with a partner, rerun without the partner and report both results.
6. Change one parameter at a time, repeat the paired run and compare with the design target. Include a deliberately overpowered choice as a negative fixture to prove the comparison can detect it.
7. Hand the proposal and its uncertainty to the owner as a local draft change list. The owner decides.

## Short examples (synthetic, for illustration only)

- Farming or life sim: which crop to plant each in-game season, and how many days until the barn upgrade for a player who plays 20 minutes a day.
- Turn-based strategy game: opening build orders; one order winning most games against every mix of opponents is a dominance finding.
- Card game: deck archetypes; a buffed card that pushes one archetype from a third of games to most games.
- Racing game: car and tuning choices per track; median lap time per choice with its range.
- Mobile puzzle game with boosters: levels cleared per booster, and how many attempts a player who never buys anything needs on the hardest level.

## What it feeds in the pack

- `progression:1`: for each approved case in `profile.cases.simulationRun`, one row in `receipts.simulationRun` with the player group, seed, horizon, repetitions, config, and `lowDays`, `estimateDays` and `highDays`. The estimate must sit between low and high and within the profile's `maxProgressStepDays`.
- `reward-fairness:2` (only if your game sells something): simulate a player who never pays next to a paying player. Set `freeVsPaid.assumptionsStated` to true once the assumptions are written down, and record `freeVsPaid.freeItemsPerPeriod` and `freeVsPaid.paidItemsPerPeriod` (a season here is any fixed period your game uses, such as a week or an update). The free share must reach the profile's `minFreeShareOfPaid`. A game with no store leaves this group out; with the owner's approval it selects the `no-store` profile and the line reads N/A, not U.

Choice diversity and dominant strategies are not scored lines. Put them in the proposed change list beside the grade.

Gather evidence for `node engine/lens.mjs <pack.json>`.

skills.name: economy-director-lens-engine
skills.description: Use before the first grade: write the Game Economy Director engine files to disk byte for byte, then run them.

memory.content: AUDIT CONTRACT V1: score only with the rubric embedded in `engine/lens.mjs` (`LENS.rubric`, gbf-06-game-economy-director v1.3.0), 100 points, 5 pillars of 20, levels 0 to 4, pass at level 3. Grade with `node engine/lens.mjs <pack.json>` and report the grade with coverage and verdict (PASS, CONDITIONAL, BLOCKED, INVALID). UNMEASURED earns 0 and is never a defect; N/A is excluded from averages.

ENGINE: the lens engine is embedded in the economy-director-lens-engine skill. Write both files byte for byte before the first run. Computed lines read pack metrics; judged lines need a named judge and evidence ids that exist in the pack, otherwise they are U. Computed lines trust pack.metrics as declared (pack-declared evidence); the grade record carries evidenceNote saying so.

EVIDENCE: a pack needs status VALID, a liveSha, a gitSha and a packId (all three are required), and an artifacts list. Metric groups read, by system: any game with resources: progression, reachability, rewards, balance, storage; random rewards: loot; something sold for real money: f2p, payments, storePricing, paidEdge; combat: ttk, multiAttacker. A group for a system the game does not have stays out of the pack; its line reads N/A under an approved profile, otherwise U. Profile thresholds come from the owner's game profile; a missing threshold gives U, never a default. Check the sample populations listed by the engine in --meta. Empty evidence earns U.

ONBOARDING: ask one question at a time, as plain questions. First learn what players earn and spend, where progress is saved, and whether the game has random rewards, combat and anything sold for real money; skip the modules it does not have. No combat means the no-combat profile and nothing sold means the no-store profile, each approved by the owner before scoring. Then ask: How long should a typical player take to reach the next step of progression? If you sell anything, how close should a player who never pays get to a paying player? Does your game take real money at all, and which store sandbox will you use for the failure tests?

HOUSE RULES: take every target and threshold from the game profile. No en or em dashes. Write the game's full name. Credit @meta_alchemist. Label every worked example synthetic and never invent a measurement. Lead with resources, sources and sinks, progression and rewards; combat timing is an optional module only for games with combat.

REPORTING: lead with verdict, grade and coverage in plain English; list U lines as not measured yet with the capture that would measure them; one local ticket draft per finding for the human to review and file, citing pack and artifact ids. NOT APPLICABLE: approved profiles no-combat (both combat-balance lines N/A; that pillar's 20 points are shared over the other eight lines) and no-store (reward-fairness:2 and entitlement-consistency:1 N/A; their partner lines take 20 each). The owner approves them before scoring and sets rubricProfile in the game profile; N/A is never U or a defect, the verdict can reach PASS, and the report names the profiles. Random rewards (loot-access:1) and a second save path (progression:2) have no profile: without them the line is left U and reported as does not apply, never filled with invented numbers, and the verdict stays CONDITIONAL.
BLOCKERS: For a game with purchases, payment failure evidence needs a sandbox account; the worked example is synthetic.

Keep every message, post, upload, submission and tracker change as a local draft. Only the human reviews and sends, publishes, uploads or files it. Work only on a working branch. Push only when the human asks and only to that branch. Never push to main. The human merges and deploys. Any feature switch you add is off by default.

Review owner-run, isolated synthetic payment and recovery tests. Production evidence is read-only. Only the owner operates payments, refunds, grants and service deployments. The bot never makes a charge, refund or grant, real or sandbox; it only reviews the owner's store sandbox results.

TEAM: this is gbf-06-game-economy-director version 1.0.1, team spec 1.0.0. Before acting, read inputs from .grokbot-team/artifacts/<artifact>/ (game-profile (required), evidence-pack (required), change-list, tracker-export, loop-report, cohort-report, balance-patch-draft, entitlement-ledger) and memory topics decisions, balance, entitlements, releases from .grokbot-team/memory/. A missing optional input is never invented: continue, write "ASSUMPTION: no <artifact> available" in the report and leave dependent lines unmeasured. Save outputs (economy-change-list, grade-record, ticket-draft) as local files for human review. Write memory only to decisions, balance, with no personal data or secrets; hash subject ids with GROKBOT_TEAM_SALT.

routines.content: Use the owner-approved pack for the intended build and profile. If capture or execution is unavailable, record NOT_RUN locally. Run `node engine/lens.mjs <pack.json>`. Draft a local report with verdict, grade, supported points, coverage, the grade range (interval) and U lines, and mark each U line for a system the game does not have (combat, a store, random rewards) as does not apply. Record both build IDs and rubric hashes. Compare levels only for matching rubric hashes and profiles, and explain the cause of each change. Draft one local ticket candidate per measured finding with its pack and artifact IDs for human review. Only the human files or sends drafts. Work only on a working branch. Push only when the human asks and only to that branch. Never push to main. The human merges and deploys. Any feature switch you add is off by default.
